page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.4xlarge is a general-purpose, burstable compute instance driven by the AWS Nitro system. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at a baseline clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 105 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16) and Intel AMX (tile and int8), facilitating hardware-accelerated numeric calculations.

System memory consists of 64.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5000 MHz, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per core). In synthetic memory testing, the instance achieved a read bandwidth of 1351.05 GB/sec on small cached blocks, while uncached 256 MB reads and writes reached 98.97 GB/sec and 75.12 GB/sec respectively. Network capacity is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. The instance provides no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached EBS volumes for persistent data needs, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded performance alongside balanced multi-core execution. The instance posted a Geekbench single-core score of 2078.0 and a multi-core score of 12210.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 27549.65. Data processing metrics show top-quartile execution in single-threaded gzip compression at 33.17 GB/sec and small-model LLM text generation at 267.15 tokens/sec. General multi-core throughput remains consistent with mid-tier general-purpose averages, yielding 16818.07 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 22.06 million operations per second in Redis SET operations.

The m7i-flex tier delivers a cost-efficient profile for moderate CPU-bound scenarios through its burstable allocation model, trading sustained maximum compute headroom for reduced operational expense compared to dedicated m7i variants. This balance positions the m7i-flex.4xlarge for application servers, microservice workloads, software compilation pipelines, middle-tier enterprise web applications, and caching nodes that do not continuously exhaust all 16 vCPUs.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.4xlarge is a general-purpose burstable instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8488C processor operating at 3.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, it provisions 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores, paired with 64.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Instruction support includes AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. The instance does not bundle local disk storage and relies on network-attached storage, supported by a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks show upper-tier single-core efficiency, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2078.0 and gzip compression throughput of 33.17 GB/sec, while multi-core compute and memory bandwidth align with mid-range baselines. The burstable CPU architecture provides a cost-effective infrastructure footprint suitable for variable-demand application hosting, Redis caching, microservices, and general backend workloads.
